name: Family / Domestic Drama
definition: Interdependent relatives or household members negotiate care, memory, obligation, and unequal power when a change makes their existing arrangement impossible to maintain.
negative_signals: romantic couple as the only central relationship
diagnostic_questions: Do several relationships change because family members depend on one another?
Does the conflict concern how a shared life will continue?

neighbors.distinction: Domestic drama distributes its central pressure across family or household relationships.
Family drama need not center one person's developmental passage.

reader_promises.name: Consequential interdependence
reader_promises.description: Make care, money, housing, history, or identity prevent easy separation.

reader_promises.name: Relational change
reader_promises.description: Resolve conflict by altering boundaries, obligations, or shared understanding rather than winning an argument.

roles.name: Family stabilizer
roles.description: Maintains routines and absorbs costs that others may not recognize.

roles.name: Disruptor
roles.description: Introduces a need, truth, return, or refusal the household cannot assimilate unchanged.

roles.name: Memory holder
roles.description: Controls a family account through testimony, silence, objects, or ritual.

stakes: Whether harm and care can be acknowledged together

movements.name: Household balance
movements.description: Establish the arrangement of care, silence, and power that currently holds.

movements.name: Disruption
movements.description: Introduce a change that makes the arrangement materially or emotionally untenable.

movements.name: Old roles fail
movements.description: Let attempts to restore normality expose hidden labor, resentment, or contradictory memory.

movements.name: New arrangement
movements.description: Resolve how people will relate, care, separate, or remember after change.

complications.name: Unequal care
complications.description: The person carrying most responsibility lacks formal authority or recognition.

complications.name: Protective family secret
complications.description: A concealment prevents one harm while perpetuating another.

complications.name: Outsider-insider
complications.description: A partner, caregiver, or adopted member sees the system clearly but has contested standing.

twists.name: Inheritance is duty
twists.description: The valuable legacy carries debt, care, or responsibility rather than freedom.

twists.name: Secret was shared
twists.description: Several relatives knew different portions and maintained silence for incompatible reasons.

conclusions.name: Renegotiated family
conclusions.description: Relationships continue under clearer and more equitable boundaries.

conclusions.name: Chosen distance
conclusions.description: Separation becomes an active form of care or self-preservation.

conclusions.name: Memory reframed
conclusions.description: The family cannot repair every relationship but changes the story it passes forward.

variation_axes.question: Whose labor or perspective was hidden?

subversions: Let reconciliation include firm distance rather than universal reunion.
Make practical redistribution of care the emotional climax.
cliches_to_avoid: One villain blamed for a system everyone maintains
A secret reveal that automatically repairs relationships
quality_checks: Every major character has a distinct need within the shared system.
The ending establishes a concrete new relational arrangement.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Popular Fiction
sources.contribution: Shows how genre stories combine plot expectations with emotional entrapment, relationships, and social difference.

sources.title: Genre as Convention and Invention
sources.contribution: Supports blending family drama with other genres while treating conventions as material for invention.
